label: thm:observability-q-independent
title: Observability is a base property: $\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0$ is independent of the substrate section
html:
Theorem. Observability is a base property: \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 is independent of the substrate section

Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) act as a QOU over the substrate line bundle \mathcal{Q}_M = M \times \mathbb{G}_m. Assume q_1, q_2 \colon M \to \mathbb{G}_m specify any two substrate sections.

Then:

  \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}_{q_1}}\!
  \bigl(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)\bigr)
  = 
  \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}_{q_2}}\!
  \bigl(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)\bigr).

If (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) sustains the observability axiom over one section q > 1, it sustains the axiom over every section, unconditionally including q = 1.

Mathematical novelty. That the Hom-spaces are independent of the differential layer d_q is a triviality; the point is that this independence carries the observability property across the transition from the regular deformed phase (q > 1) to the singular substrate (q = 1).
